action_summary: `_extract_capability_feature_flags` refused a capability for `writes_fixed_repo_tmp_under_ro_input` whenever any adapter source CONTAINED a `canonical/tmp_*` string literal. Measured 2026-11-03/04: all 19 capabilities refused on that ground use the literal only as a caller-overridable fallback -- `str(raw or "canonical/tmp_...")` or `fresh_output(repo, args.get("output_path"), "canonical/tmp_...")`, whose second parameter exists to override the third -- and none writes it unconditionally. On the onboarding path the adapter's root is `/work/repo` (writable, per run), not the read-only `/input`. With the refusal lifted for those 19, FIFTEEN onboard on two genuinely passing runs with distinct binds; the four that cannot pass still fail (NO_GENUINELY_PASSING_RUNS, WALLCLOCK_LIMIT_EXCEEDED). The static guess was pre-empting the runtime authority that was going to judge the write anyway. It is replaced by a test of UNCONDITIONAL writes, so the genuine protection is kept and narrowed to the truth.

The creature's sampler always supplies output_path so it is unreachable in practice, but a direct caller that omits it collides across concurrent runs. Rewriting them to use a per-run temp directory is the follow-up and is not done here, because it is 19 adapter edits with no capability gain over this change.

weakens_existing_guard: A refusal is narrowed, and this must be stated plainly rather than argued away: capabilities that were previously refused statically are now attempted. The justification is measurement, not convenience -- 15 of 19 demonstrate two genuinely passing runs with distinct binds, and the 4 that cannot pass are still refused by the onboarding gate. Nothing about the onboarding gate's own criteria is relaxed; no tolerance is widened; the confined worker still runs every adapter against a read-only `/input`. The residual risk is that the 19 wrappers write a fixed path when a caller supplies no output argument, which the sampler always supplies; that is recorded as a latent defect below rather than fixed here.
